title: subagent agent.json
description: The settings file of one agent folder under tools.native.subagent.agents_dir (Go backend only). Every key is optional: a folder may hold only prompt.md. The agent name is the folder name. The same keys are accepted inline under tools.native.subagent.agents.<name> in setting.json. Relative paths in model and prompt_documents resolve from the folder that holds this file.

description.description: Shown to the model in the tool description, so keep it short.

model.description: Model for this agent. In a catalog-layout session a value that does not end in .json is a model ID '<category>/<name>' of the models catalog; the agent may name any model of it, not only those its caller's profile lists. A value ending in .json is a model file, relative to the agent's folder and must stay inside it (no .., absolute path or symlink leaving the folder). A legacy session reads every value as a file path (relative to the session directory for an inline agent). Absent means the calling session's model.

instructions.description: System prompt of the agent. The calling session's prompt is not used.

prompt_documents.description: Files appended to the agent's prompt after instructions (and after prompt.md for a folder agent), each separated by a blank line. A relative path is taken from the session's cwd, or from the agent's folder for a folder agent; ~ is expanded. The files are read when the session loads, and a missing file is a configuration error. The calling session's own prompt_documents are not used.

tools.description: Tools the agent may use: enabled tools by name (read, grep, glob, fetch, skill, decide_systemone, web_search, and write, edit, bash, exec and process, which the agent's list alone grants; a child that lists process sees and stops only the processes it started, and they are stopped when its run ends), and, by name only, subagent, tool_smith, profile_message and load_tool when the session enables them (load_tool only for a child of a profile with tools.lazy) (profile_message also needs another profile to message; with a toolset, both come from the session, not from the toolset), and MCP tools by ID, written mcp:<server>:<tool> (the server id from mcp_servers and the tool name the server reports). Absent means every enabled read-only native or extension tool and no MCP tool. An MCP tool is never added because its server calls it read-only: you name each one, so you vouch that it cannot change anything you care about. mcp:<server>:* gives the agent every loaded tool of that server (each once, even if also named exactly); a wildcard that matches no tool is a configuration error naming the server. An agent that lists write, edit, bash or exec runs them at once like the session does, takes the checkpoint like a write, and runs to its end instead of being handed off unless tools.native.subagent.background_writers is on. A name that is not loaded is a configuration error that lists the loaded ones; it is checked when the session loads.

toolset.description: One toolset file or a list of them, each '<category>/<name>' under the tools catalog (catalog-layout session only). The agent takes its tools, with their settings, and its MCP servers from it (or them) instead of the session's own toolset, so the profile does not have to register them and the parent never sees them. 'tools' still narrows within it and its mcp:<server>:<tool> entries are resolved against this file's servers only. The profile's tools.deny and each tool's own paths still apply. The toolset's own subagent entry is ignored; an agent that names a toolset may still list subagent, which is the session's tool. A sub-agent's toolset must not set tools.native.profile_message. An unknown toolset is a configuration error that lists the available ones. Given a list, the toolsets merge in order: when two name the same native tool or MCP server the first listed wins, with a warning, and only the first toolset with hooks supplies hooks (a later one's hooks are ignored with a warning). Absent means the session's toolset.

max_tool_rounds.description: Most tool rounds of one run.

max_run_tokens.description: Most tokens one run may use before it starts another provider round. Absent means no cap.

auto_compaction.description: Whether this agent's child compacts its own transcript when it grows. Absent follows the session's compaction.auto_enabled, or is on when compaction_trigger_tokens is set.

compaction_trigger_tokens.description: Input size, in tokens, at which this agent's child compacts. Absent uses the session's compaction.trigger_tokens, which is sized for the master's model, so set it for a model with a different context window or price. Not allowed with auto_compaction false.

state_context.description: Send the newest state-context block stored for the session to this agent's child, in every request. A child collects none of its own. Nothing is sent when the session's statecontext is off or has no block yet.

isolation.description: none (default) runs the child in the session's working directory. worktree runs each run in a git worktree of its own, on a new branch (worktree.branch_prefix + run id) made from HEAD; the session's uncommitted changes are not in it. When the run ends, whatever it left is committed to the branch and the worktree folder is removed; the branch stays when the run changed something and is deleted otherwise, and the result names it with its diff stat. A worktree run changes no file of the session, so it needs no checkpoint and may run beside other runs as an async handle; the path rules apply to the same paths inside the worktree. MCP tools still act on the session's own folder. A resume starts from the branch of the run it continues. Needs a tool that changes files and a working directory inside a git repository with a commit.

read_only.description: true makes every exec call of the agent a read_only one, whatever the model sends, so exec does not make it an agent that changes files: a call to it needs no checkpoint and may run beside other calls or as an async handle. Under a bwrap or seatbelt sandbox its exec calls get sandbox.plan_writable_paths (by default only the temp folder) and cannot write the project; without a sandbox it is the agent's promise. Needs exec in tools and no other tool that changes files (tool_smith, subagent, profile_message); not with isolation worktree.

timeout_ms.description: Wall-clock limit of one run, including provider waits.
